items.title: South Korea tests Arctic shipping route amid Russia-West row
items.summary: For South Korean ships, navigating off north coast of Russia dramatically reduces travel time to Europe, but the pro-Ukraine coalition might see it as undermining their efforts to isolate Moscow A South Korean container ship completed a voyage to Western Europe through the Arctic Ocean off the northern coast of Russia in October, fueling Seoul's hopes of exploiting the route as a shortcut for trade The ship made the round trip from Busan to Rotterdam in just 50 days, saving at least 10 days compared to the fastest travel times along the more commonly used Suez Canal route. The Northern Sea Route (NSR) is not only around 7,000 kilometers (4,350 miles) shorter, it also avoids the geopolitical flashpoint of the Middle East But the faster delivery times might not exactly trigger celebrations across western European capitals Analysts say the nations arrayed against Russia over its invasion of Ukraine fear that South Korean President Lee Jae-myung is looking to boost Seoul's economic relations with Moscow.

items.title: Mozambique: Fuel import bill surges 79.4% in Q2
items.summary: Statistical data from the Bank of Mozambique indicate that fuel imports amounted to US$236.4 million (€203.5 million) in the first quarter and US$424.2 million (€365.1 million) in the second This represented a 79.4% increase in Mozambique’s fuel import bill from the first to the second quarter, a period marked by fuel supply difficulties in several regions of the country and constraints on access to foreign currency to finance imports In April and May, long queues formed at filling stations, some petrol stations were temporarily closed, and supply difficulties affected transport operators, businesses and consumers Over the same six-month period, Mozambique imported intermediate goods worth a total of US$1,198.7 million (€1,031.5 million), with fuels accounting for around 55% of this import category On 7 May, the Government decided to increase fuel prices, with the price of diesel rising by 45.5% and petrol by 12.1%.

items.title: Mozambique: Private sector returns to growth in October, PMI shows
items.summary: Mozambique’s private sector regained momentum in October, as new orders rose at the sharpest pace in over five years and lifted business activity back into growth. Firms responded by raising their input purchases at a record rate However, stronger demand also added to cost pressures, with purchase prices rising at the quickest pace in nearly four-and-a-half years. Business optimism nonetheless remained historically elevated, despite easing slightly from September’s near nine-year high The headline figure derived from the survey is the Purchasing Managers’ IndexTM (PMI®). Readings above 50.0 signal an improvement in business conditions on the previous month, while readings below 50.0 show a deterioration The Mozambique PMI recorded above the 50.0 neutral threshold for the fourth consecutive month in October, signalling a further improvement in private sector operating conditions.

items.title: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years

items.title: Government to mobilize about 27 billion meticais for mitigation of El Niño
items.summary: Maputo, 05 Nov (AIM) – The Mozambican government plans to mobilize approximately 27 billion meticais (1.7 billion US dollars at the current exchange rate) to implement the 2026/27 National Plan for Mitigating the Impacts of El Niño weather phenomenon. The plan aims to cover sectors of agriculture, health, education, water supply, food assistance, and social protection sectors. According to the Prime Minister Benvinda Levi, who was speaking on Wednesday at the country’s parliament, Assembly of the Republic, in response to concerns raised by parliamentary groups, the measure is also aimed at distributing agricultural input kits to over 185,000 households, incusing the construction of multi-purpose silos to complement small-scale irrigation systems, and the rehabilitation or construction of dams, water supply systems, and multi-purpose boreholes, “all aimed at benefiting more than one million people.” The 2026/27 rainy season points to normal rainfall in the Northern provinces of Nampula, Cabo Delgado, and Niassa.

items.title: Frelimo Extraordinary Session to take place on November 27-28
items.summary: Maputo, 05 Nov (AIM) – Mozambique’s ruling Frelimo Party has announced that the 5th Extraordinary Session of its Central Committee will take place on November 27–28 at the party’s Central School in Matola city, southern Maputo province. According to the party’s Central Committee spokesperson, Pedro Guiliche – speaking following an Ordinary Session of the Political Commission, which was chaired by the party’s President Daniel Chapo – the party will focus on three main agenda items: the review and approval of the directive on internal elections for party bodies; the Code of Ethical Conduct and Party Discipline; and the theses for the 13th Congress. The approval of these instruments is part of the preparations for the 13th Congress, scheduled to take place from July 20 to 25, 2027, in the northern city of Nampula.

items.title: Several European flights receive bomb threats, some divert
items.summary: Several flights across Europe have either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris; more soon followed Several commercial flights made either unscheduled or high-alert landings in France, Italy, Belgium and Bulgaria, according to authorities in the various countries Planes made unscheduled landings in Evreux, France; and in Bulgaria.

items.title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK
items.summary: DR Congo has been facing the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history A British man who has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo will be flown back to the UK It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths It is not clear when the flight will take place Earlier, a UK government spokesperson said there were "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and that the risk to the public remains low Reuters news agency reported the infected man is a healthcare worker, citing an internal document BBC News has not seen Imported Ebola cases are extremely rare in the UK and have resulted in no deaths There have only been four confirmed cases of the virus in the UK - one, in 1976, resulting from a laboratory incident, and three involving health workers who were responding to an outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015 A UK government spokesperson said: "The UK has well-established procedures for…

items.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
items.summary: More than 500 parties are contesting the elections South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC) This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern.
